newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** Indian finance minister P. Chidambaram has said that a controversial corporate tax may be phased out after a new Income Tax Act and Companies Act came into force, the Financial Express reports.

"The introduction of MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax) in the last budget has caused a high degree of discomfort to industry. It was introduced as a number of companies were paying dividend but not tax," he told a seminar organised by the International Association of Lawyers on Sunday, the paper says.
Chidambaram's speech was also reported by other Indian newspapers on Monday.
** The Congress Working Committee will hold a crucial meeting on Wednesday to review the performance of the government, the Hindustan Times says.
Announcing this, Congress president Sitaram Kesri said the party would thereafter, if necessary, rethink about its support to the government, the paper reports.
Kesri, however, made it clear that at the present moment the question of withdrawing support to the government did not arise.
** The Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) new takeover code is not expected to be in place before the next two months, the Business Standard says.
The code is also unlikely to give up the 20 percent minimum public offer clause despite demands for 100 percent mandatory offers, the paper reports.
** Issuers have silently raised close to 250 billion rupees in the last 21 months through the private placement route, largely in the form of debt, the Economic Times reports.
This figure is much higher than the 170 billion rupees raised in the same period through the public issue or the retail route, the paper says.
** Maruti Udyog Ltd (MUL) plans to float a $250 million issue on the overseas capital markets in the middle of next year, the Business Standard reports.
The proceeds from the issue, which would not be convertible into Indian equity, would be used to fund MUL's capacity expansion and modernisation plans, the paper says.
However, the company has yet to decide whether to go to the Euro-markets or adopt the American Depository Receipts route.
** The Bombay Stock Exchange's top 30-share index .BSESN rose 54.95 points, or 1.94 percent last week from the previous week, at 2,881.165. But the underlying trend remains shaky, market players say.
